text: APT29 (Cozy Bear) conducted a sustained espionage campaign targeting government agencies and critical infrastructure using custom backdoors and credential harvesting tools. The group exploited CVE-2023-42793 in JetBrains TeamCity to gain initial access, then deployed GraphicalProton and other bespoke implants for persistence.

LockBit 3.0 ransomware variant was deployed against healthcare and financial sector organizations, encrypting systems and exfiltrating sensitive patient data for double extortion. The operators leveraged compromised RDP credentials and Cobalt Strike beacons for lateral movement before deploying the ransomware payload.

A sophisticated phishing campaign impersonated Microsoft 365 account recovery emails, harvesting credentials through adversary-in-the-middle proxy infrastructure. The operation used Evilginx2 to bypass MFA and captured session tokens, compromising over 1,200 corporate accounts globally.

CVE-2024-3400 in Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS GlobalProtect gateway allowed unauthenticated remote code execution via command injection. Threat actors exploited this zero-day in the wild to deploy reverse shells and exfiltrate firewall configurations, CVSS score 10.0.

A supply chain compromise was discovered in the XZ Utils library (CVE-2024-3094), where a malicious maintainer introduced a backdoor into versions 5.6.0 and 5.6.1. The backdoor targeted SSH authentication on Debian and RPM-based systems, enabling unauthorized remote access.

APT28 (Fancy Bear) exploited CVE-2023-23397 in Microsoft Outlook to relay NTLM hashes without user interaction. The campaign targeted defense and energy sectors across NATO member states, using the stolen credentials to access Exchange mailboxes and SharePoint sites.

BlackCat (ALPHV) ransomware affiliates targeted a major US healthcare payment processor, disrupting claims processing nationwide. The attackers gained access via stolen credentials to a Citrix remote access portal lacking MFA, then deployed ransomware after 9 days of lateral movement.

Volt Typhoon, a Chinese state-sponsored group, maintained persistent access to US critical infrastructure using living-off-the-land techniques. The group leveraged compromised SOHO routers as operational relay nodes and used built-in Windows tools like netsh, PowerShell, and wmic to avoid detection.

A zero-day vulnerability in Ivanti Connect Secure VPN (CVE-2024-21887) allowed authenticated command injection, chained with CVE-2023-46805 authentication bypass for unauthenticated RCE. Multiple threat actors exploited these in the wild to deploy web shells and steal configuration data.

A QR code phishing campaign (quishing) targeted corporate employees via fake parking violation notices and HR benefits enrollment emails. Victims scanning the QR codes were directed to credential harvesting pages mimicking Azure AD login portals, successfully compromising accounts at 47 organizations.

Scattered Spider (UNC3944) conducted social engineering attacks against IT help desks, convincing staff to reset MFA for high-privilege accounts. The group then used the compromised identities to access cloud management consoles and deploy ransomware across VMware ESXi environments.

Play ransomware operators exploited CVE-2024-55591 in FortiOS to gain super_admin privileges on FortiGate firewalls. After disabling security controls, they moved laterally using PsExec and deployed ransomware to domain-joined systems, demanding 4.5 million USD in cryptocurrency.

A supply chain attack compromised the build pipeline of a popular Python package on PyPI, injecting a cryptocurrency miner and credential stealer into the distributed package. Over 170,000 downloads occurred before the malicious version was identified and removed.

APT41 (Winnti) deployed a new variant of the ShadowPad backdoor targeting semiconductor manufacturers in Taiwan and South Korea. The group exploited CVE-2024-24576 in Rust standard library on Windows to achieve argument injection, using it as an initial access vector.

CVE-2024-47575 in Fortinet FortiManager allowed unauthenticated remote code execution via the FGFM protocol. Dubbed FortiJump, this zero-day was actively exploited by UNC5820 to exfiltrate FortiGate device configurations containing sensitive credentials and firewall rules.

Akira ransomware group targeted mid-sized enterprises by exploiting Cisco ASA/FTD VPN vulnerabilities (CVE-2023-20269) for initial access. The operators used Mimikatz and LaZagne for credential dumping before encrypting both Windows and Linux systems with their cross-platform ransomware.

A business email compromise campaign used deepfake audio to impersonate CFOs during phone calls, authorizing fraudulent wire transfers. The attackers first compromised email accounts via phishing, then used AI-generated voice cloning to confirm payment instructions, netting over 25 million USD.

Lazarus Group conducted Operation DreamJob, targeting aerospace and defense engineers with fake LinkedIn job offers. The malicious attachments deployed the LightlessCan RAT, a sophisticated HTTP-based implant with over 68 commands for espionage and data exfiltration.

CVE-2025-0282 in Ivanti Connect Secure allowed unauthenticated stack-based buffer overflow leading to remote code execution. Chinese state-sponsored actors chained this with CVE-2025-0283 for privilege escalation, deploying the SPAWNMOLE tunneler and SPAWNSNAIL SSH backdoor.

A malicious GitHub Action (tj-actions/changed-files) was compromised via a supply chain attack, leaking CI/CD secrets from over 23,000 repositories. The injected code exfiltrated environment variables including AWS keys, npm tokens, and GitHub PATs to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

Medusa ransomware group escalated attacks against education and healthcare, leveraging initial access brokers for compromised VPN and RDP credentials. The group maintained a Tor-based leak site and imposed 48-hour payment deadlines, with ransoms ranging from 100K to 15 million USD.

APT44 (Sandworm) deployed AcidPour, a new Linux wiper variant targeting RAID arrays and LVM volumes in Ukrainian telecommunications infrastructure. The malware overwrites critical filesystem structures before triggering a reboot, rendering systems unrecoverable.

A credential phishing kit called Tycoon 2FA was sold on Telegram, enabling adversary-in-the-middle attacks to bypass MFA on Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace. The kit rotated phishing domains every 4 hours and used Cloudflare Turnstile to evade automated analysis.

CVE-2024-4577 in PHP CGI on Windows allowed remote code execution via argument injection when running in certain language locales. Multiple threat actors mass-exploited internet-facing PHP servers within 48 hours of disclosure, deploying cryptominers and web shells.

RansomHub emerged as a major ransomware-as-a-service operation, recruiting affiliates from disbanded ALPHV and LockBit groups. The variant featured Golang and C++ payloads, ESXi encryptor support, and an aggressive affiliate model offering 90 percent revenue share.

Turla (Snake) was observed using hijacked Starlink connections and compromised satellite internet terminals as command-and-control relay infrastructure. The group targeted diplomatic entities in Central Asia, deploying an updated version of their Kazuar .NET backdoor.

A supply chain compromise affected the Polyfill.io CDN domain after its acquisition by a Chinese entity. Malicious JavaScript was injected into over 100,000 websites, redirecting mobile users to scam sites and harvesting form data from legitimate pages.

CVE-2025-21298 in Windows OLE allowed remote code execution via specially crafted RTF documents opened in Microsoft Outlook. The vulnerability required no user interaction beyond previewing the email, with CVSS score 9.8. Exploitation was observed targeting financial institutions.

Cl0p ransomware group exploited zero-day vulnerabilities in Cleo Harmony, VLTrader, and LexiCom file transfer products (CVE-2024-50623) for mass data theft. The campaign followed the group's established pattern of targeting managed file transfer solutions, affecting over 60 organizations.

A spear-phishing campaign targeted energy sector executives using fake DOE correspondence about renewable energy grants. The emails contained ISO images with embedded LNK files that executed PowerShell downloaders, deploying the Brute Ratel C4 post-exploitation framework.

APT35 (Charming Kitten) deployed a custom PowerShell-based keylogger dubbed CharmPower against think tanks and academic researchers studying Middle Eastern geopolitics. Initial access was gained via watering hole attacks on compromised academic journal websites.

Black Basta ransomware operators adopted a new social engineering technique, flooding employee inboxes with subscription spam then calling posing as IT help desk to install AnyDesk or Quick Assist. This living-off-the-land approach bypassed email security controls.

A zero-day in Atlassian Confluence Data Center (CVE-2024-21683) allowed authenticated RCE via code macro injection. APT groups exploited this within Confluence instances accessible from the internet to establish footholds in technology companies and deploy Sliver C2 implants.

A compromised npm package (event-stream successor) contained an obfuscated dependency targeting cryptocurrency wallet applications. The supply chain attack specifically activated when detecting Copay wallet build environments, exfiltrating private keys to attacker infrastructure.

Kimsuky (APT43) launched a credential harvesting campaign against South Korean defense contractors using fake DAPA procurement portal login pages. Stolen credentials were used to access classified project documents related to next-generation fighter aircraft programs.

INC Ransom deployed a new Linux variant targeting VMware ESXi 8.0 hypervisors, encrypting VMDK files and deleting snapshots. The group used stolen vCenter credentials and SSH to access ESXi hosts directly, bypassing endpoint detection tools that do not cover hypervisor layers.

A large-scale SMS phishing (smishing) campaign impersonated USPS, UPS, and FedEx delivery notifications across North America. Victims were directed to fake tracking pages that harvested credit card numbers and installed Android banking trojans via sideloaded APK files.

CVE-2025-24472 in FortiOS and FortiProxy allowed unauthenticated attackers to gain super_admin privileges via crafted CSF proxy requests. The vulnerability was chained with CVE-2024-55591 in active exploitation campaigns to fully compromise FortiGate perimeter firewalls.

A supply chain attack on the 3CX desktop application distributed trojanized installers signed with a valid code signing certificate. The compromised application loaded a malicious DLL that contacted GitHub-hosted C2 infrastructure, deploying an information stealer targeting browser credentials.

APT40 (Leviathan) targeted maritime and shipbuilding industries in the South China Sea region, exploiting CVE-2024-38063 in the Windows TCP/IP stack for initial access. The group deployed ScanBox reconnaissance framework and custom PlugX variants for persistent espionage operations.

APT32 (OceanLotus) launched a targeted espionage campaign against Southeast Asian government ministries and foreign embassies. The group used malicious Microsoft Office documents with embedded macros to deliver the Denis backdoor, leveraging Cloudflare Workers for C2 communication to blend with legitimate traffic.

APT10 (Stone Panda) conducted a prolonged espionage operation targeting managed service providers across Europe and North America. The group abused legitimate cloud services for data staging and exfiltrated intellectual property from MSP client networks using the Quasar RAT and custom loaders.

Gamaredon (Primitive Bear) intensified cyber operations against Ukrainian government entities and NGOs, deploying the GammaSteel infostealer via USB-propagated malware. The group used Telegram channels as dead-drop resolvers for C2 infrastructure, rotating IP addresses every 30 minutes to evade blocking.

Mustang Panda (Bronze President) targeted European diplomatic organizations with PlugX malware variants concealed within RAR archives masquerading as EU policy documents. The group used DLL side-loading via legitimate signed executables and established persistence through scheduled tasks with encoded PowerShell commands.

SideWinder APT group targeted military and government institutions in Pakistan and Sri Lanka using spear-phishing emails with weaponized RTF documents exploiting the Equation Editor vulnerability. The group deployed a custom .NET implant for keylogging, screen capture, and document theft operations.

Winnti Group (APT41 subcluster) compromised multiple gaming companies through a supply chain attack on a widely used game development SDK. The trojanized SDK injected a kernel-level rootkit into game client builds, enabling cryptomining and credential theft from millions of end-user systems.

APT38 (Bluenoroff) executed a sophisticated SWIFT banking fraud campaign against financial institutions in Southeast Asia. The group compromised payment switch applications through watering hole attacks on banking industry forums, manipulating transaction records to redirect over 45 million USD in wire transfers.

Lapsus$ (DEV-0537) resurfaced with attacks on major technology companies, using social engineering and SIM swapping to compromise employee accounts. The group accessed internal source code repositories and published stolen data on Telegram, demonstrating continued risk from loosely organized extortion groups.

RansomHub affiliates exploited CVE-2024-6387 (regreSSHion) in OpenSSH to gain initial access to Linux servers at multiple hosting providers. After establishing persistence via cron jobs and SSH authorized keys, the group deployed their cross-platform ransomware encrypting both Linux and Windows systems within the hybrid environments.

Rhysida ransomware group conducted a devastating attack against a major US hospital network, encrypting electronic health record systems and exfiltrating patient data. The group demanded 4.2 million USD in Bitcoin and published a portion of stolen records including surgical images and psychiatric evaluations on their leak site.

Cactus ransomware operators exploited Qlik Sense vulnerabilities (CVE-2023-41266 and CVE-2023-41265) for initial access into enterprise business intelligence environments. The group uniquely self-encrypted their ransomware binary to evade antivirus detection and used 7-Zip for data staging before exfiltration via rclone.

Royal ransomware rebranded as BlackSuit and escalated attacks against critical infrastructure, particularly the manufacturing and water utility sectors. The group used callback phishing to establish initial contact, followed by deployment of SystemBC proxy malware and Cobalt Strike for lateral movement before encryption.

Trigona ransomware operators targeted Microsoft SQL Server databases exposed to the internet, brute-forcing SA accounts and using xp_cmdshell for initial command execution. The group deployed their Delphi-based encryptor after exfiltrating database contents and Active Directory credentials via Impacket tools.

BianLian ransomware group shifted entirely to data extortion without encryption, targeting law firms handling major corporate mergers. The group exploited ProxyShell vulnerabilities in on-premises Exchange servers and used WinSCP for data exfiltration, threatening to leak privileged attorney-client communications.

NoEscape ransomware, a rebrand of the former Avaddon operation, targeted European manufacturing companies using initial access purchased from underground forums. The group deployed triple extortion combining data encryption, data theft, and DDoS threats against victim web infrastructure to maximize payment pressure.

Snatch ransomware group exploited the technique of rebooting Windows systems into Safe Mode before deploying their encryptor, disabling endpoint security solutions that do not load in Safe Mode. The group targeted construction and engineering firms, exfiltrating architectural plans and financial records before encryption.

Vice Society continued targeting the education sector with multiple ransomware variants including BlackCat and Zeppelin. The group customized ransom demands based on perceived victim revenue and released detailed internal communications from school districts to pressure payment from local government entities.

CVE-2024-23897 in Jenkins CLI allowed unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files via the args4j argument parsing library. Threat actors exploited this to extract Jenkins secrets, SSH keys, and build pipeline credentials, leading to downstream supply chain compromises of software produced by affected CI/CD environments.

CVE-2024-6387 (regreSSHion) was a critical signal handler race condition in OpenSSH server affecting glibc-based Linux systems. The vulnerability allowed unauthenticated remote code execution as root, representing a regression of CVE-2006-5051. Over 14 million internet-facing OpenSSH servers were potentially vulnerable at disclosure.

CVE-2024-27198 in JetBrains TeamCity allowed unauthenticated administrative access via an authentication bypass in the web interface. Multiple APT groups including APT29 and financially motivated actors mass-exploited the vulnerability to compromise CI/CD build servers and inject malicious code into software build pipelines.

CVE-2025-24813 in Apache Tomcat allowed remote code execution through deserialization of untrusted data via partial PUT requests. Attackers targeted internet-facing Java web applications to deploy memory-resident web shells that persisted across application restarts by injecting into session serialization files.

CVE-2024-20353 in Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance allowed unauthenticated denial of service and was chained with CVE-2024-20359 for persistent backdoor implantation. The exploitation campaign dubbed ArcaneDoor was attributed to a state-sponsored actor targeting government networks through perimeter network devices.

A watering hole attack compromised the website of a major European aviation safety regulator, injecting a malicious iframe that delivered a browser exploit targeting CVE-2024-4947 in Chrome V8. The campaign selectively activated only for visitors from defense and aerospace IP ranges, deploying a fileless backdoor into browser process memory.

A sophisticated watering hole campaign compromised industry-specific forums used by industrial control system engineers. Visitors to the compromised sites were served the ScanBox JavaScript reconnaissance framework, which profiled browser plugins, installed software, and internal network configurations to identify high-value targets for follow-on exploitation.

A large-scale credential stuffing campaign targeted financial services APIs using credentials sourced from stealer log marketplaces. Attackers used residential proxy networks and headless browsers to bypass rate limiting and WAF protections, successfully compromising over 35,000 accounts at banks and cryptocurrency exchanges within a two-week period.

Automated credential stuffing attacks targeted enterprise VPN portals and SaaS applications using credential pairs harvested from Raccoon Stealer and Redline Stealer infections. The campaign leveraged CAPTCHA-solving services and distributed attack infrastructure across cloud providers to evade IP-based blocking mechanisms.

An SEO poisoning campaign manipulated search engine results for popular software downloads including Blender, GIMP, and Notepad++. Malicious advertisements and cloned websites ranked above legitimate results, distributing trojanized installers bundled with the IcedID loader and leading to Cobalt Strike deployment.

A sustained SEO poisoning campaign targeted IT administrators searching for network management tools and system utilities. Compromised WordPress sites were injected with SEO spam pages ranking for terms like 'PuTTY download' and 'WinSCP installer', delivering the Nitrogen malware loader that deployed BlackCat ransomware.

Malvertising campaigns abused Google Ads and Bing Ads platforms to distribute fake download pages for enterprise software including Zoom, Webex, and Slack. The malicious ads appeared at the top of search results and delivered BatLoader, which installed the Redline information stealer and established Cobalt Strike persistence.

A malvertising operation targeting macOS users distributed trojanized DMG files masquerading as the Arc browser and Notion productivity app. The campaign used legitimate ad networks to serve malicious ads on tech news websites, delivering the Atomic Stealer (AMOS) macOS infostealer targeting browser passwords, cryptocurrency wallets, and keychain credentials.

A series of malicious npm packages mimicking popular libraries through typosquatting were discovered deploying reverse shells and cryptocurrency miners. Packages named 'lod-ash', 'axois', and 'reacct-dom' collectively accumulated over 500,000 downloads before detection, with the malicious code activating only during CI/CD pipeline execution to avoid developer scrutiny.

A supply chain attack poisoned multiple PyPI packages targeting machine learning and data science workflows. The malicious packages included trojanized versions of popular ML utility libraries that exfiltrated AWS credentials, model training data, and Jupyter notebook contents to attacker-controlled S3 buckets during package installation.

Attackers compromised a CI/CD pipeline at a major SaaS provider by exploiting misconfigured GitHub Actions self-hosted runners. The compromised runners enabled the injection of backdoor code into production builds, affecting downstream customers. The technique mirrored the Codecov attack pattern of exfiltrating secrets from the build environment.

A Codecov-style supply chain attack compromised a popular code coverage reporting tool used by thousands of open source projects. The attackers modified the bash uploader script to exfiltrate CI environment variables including GitHub tokens, AWS keys, and Docker Hub credentials, enabling cascading access to dependent repositories.

APT35 (Charming Kitten) launched a multi-stage campaign against nuclear energy researchers using a fake conference registration portal. The campaign delivered the BellaCiao .NET backdoor through macro-enabled documents and leveraged DNS tunneling for covert C2 communication, exfiltrating research documents over months.

APT32 (OceanLotus) targeted journalists and human rights organizations investigating labor conditions in Southeast Asia. The group deployed a new macOS backdoor distributed through trojanized chat applications, using steganography to embed C2 instructions within image files posted on social media platforms.

Gamaredon escalated operations with a new USB worm variant that spread across air-gapped networks in Ukrainian critical infrastructure. The worm created hidden directories on removable media, masking malicious executables as document files, and exfiltrated data by writing it to USB drives that were later connected to internet-facing systems.

Mustang Panda deployed the TONESHELL backdoor against telecommunications providers in the Philippines and Indonesia. The group used a novel DLL hollowing technique to inject malicious code into legitimate Windows binaries, establishing persistence through COM object hijacking that survived system reboots and updates.

SideWinder APT expanded operations beyond South Asia, targeting diplomatic missions and maritime industry organizations in the Mediterranean region. The group leveraged server-side polymorphism to generate unique malware payloads for each victim, complicating signature-based detection and threat intelligence correlation efforts.

APT38 (Bluenoroff) executed a cryptocurrency heist targeting DeFi protocols by deploying fake trading applications to blockchain developers. The trojanized applications contained a backdoored Electron framework that stole private keys and seed phrases, resulting in thefts totaling over 80 million USD across multiple decentralized finance platforms.

Lapsus$ affiliated actors targeted a major identity provider through social engineering of customer support representatives. The attackers bypassed security verification by providing previously stolen personal information and gained access to administrative tools, enabling downstream compromise of customer single sign-on configurations.

RansomHub operators deployed EDR killer tools based on the Terminator driver (zemana) to disable CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, and Microsoft Defender before ransomware deployment. The BYOVD technique used a legitimately signed but vulnerable kernel driver to terminate protected security processes with kernel-level privileges.

A watering hole attack targeted the website of a water utility industry association, compromising its member portal with a JavaScript-based exploit chain. The attack delivered a custom implant to visitors from registered IP ranges of water treatment facilities, enabling reconnaissance of SCADA network topologies.

A credential stuffing campaign leveraged a botnet of over 200,000 compromised IoT devices to target cloud-based email services. The distributed attack bypassed traditional rate limiting by spreading login attempts across the massive bot pool, successfully compromising accounts used for payroll systems and initiating fraudulent payment redirections.

An SEO poisoning campaign created thousands of fake pages on compromised legitimate websites targeting searches for government forms and tax filing software. Victims downloading the poisoned documents received the Gootloader JavaScript-based malware framework, which deployed Cobalt Strike and facilitated REvil ransomware delivery.

A malvertising campaign exploited programmatic advertising networks to deliver exploit kits through legitimate news websites. The RIG exploit kit targeted unpatched browsers to deliver the SocGholish fake browser update framework, which served as an initial access vector for the WastedLocker ransomware group across corporate environments.

A supply chain attack targeted the Gradle build system plugin ecosystem, injecting malicious code into a widely used Android development plugin. The compromised plugin exfiltrated signing keys and source code from Android application builds, affecting over 3,000 applications on the Google Play Store before detection.

Winnti Group launched a campaign targeting pharmaceutical companies conducting COVID antiviral research, deploying the Winnti4 backdoor through a compromised patch management system. The attackers achieved persistence in the software update infrastructure, enabling them to selectively push malware only to targeted research laboratories.

Rhysida ransomware exploited CVE-2024-37085 in VMware ESXi Active Directory integration to gain administrative access to hypervisor clusters. After creating the ESX Admins AD group with attacker-controlled credentials, the group encrypted virtual machine disk files across the entire virtualization infrastructure of a government agency.

Cactus ransomware operators targeted enterprise VPN concentrators by exploiting CVE-2024-20353 in Cisco ASA to establish initial access. The group used a unique approach of encrypting their ransomware payload with AES keys derived from the victim's machine identity, making static analysis and sandbox detonation of the samples impossible.

A watering hole attack compromised a legal industry news portal to target attorneys at firms handling national security litigation. The exploit chain leveraged CVE-2025-2783 in Chrome to escape the sandbox and deploy the DevilsTongue spyware, collecting privileged legal communications and client case files.

A massive credential stuffing operation targeted healthcare patient portals across the United States, testing billions of credential pairs harvested from infostealer malware. Compromised patient accounts were used to order fraudulent prescriptions and access protected health information for insurance fraud and identity theft schemes.

An npm supply chain attack injected a sophisticated backdoor into a widely used JavaScript validation library. The malicious code activated only in production environments by detecting NODE_ENV variables, establishing encrypted C2 channels and providing remote shell access to application servers processing sensitive customer payment data.

APT10 (Stone Panda) compromised a major cloud hosting provider through spear-phishing of privileged administrators, then pivoted to customer environments using stolen API keys. The group exfiltrated intellectual property from defense contractors and technology companies hosted on the platform over a six-month dwell time.

A malvertising campaign leveraged deepfake video advertisements featuring AI-generated celebrity endorsements to lure victims to fake investment platforms. The fraudulent platforms deployed browser-based cryptominers and harvested financial credentials, collectively stealing over 12 million USD from victims across North America and Europe.

Vice Society affiliates targeted a major European transportation authority, encrypting ticketing systems and operational management platforms. The attack caused multi-day disruptions to public transit schedules and exposed personal data of millions of commuters, with the group threatening data release unless a 3 million EUR ransom was paid.

A compromised CI/CD pipeline at a major container registry injected cryptomining code into popular base Docker images. Over 40 official images were affected for a 72-hour window before detection, potentially impacting thousands of downstream container deployments across cloud environments globally.

Snatch ransomware operators targeted managed service providers in a campaign to maximize downstream impact. After compromising the MSP's remote monitoring and management tools, the group deployed ransomware simultaneously across 28 of the MSP's clients, encrypting systems and demanding individual ransoms from each affected organization.

A watering hole campaign compromised financial industry conference websites to target attendees from central banks and financial regulators. The injected JavaScript fingerprinted visitors and delivered tailored exploits only to targets matching specific organizational email domains, deploying a custom Go-based RAT for long-term surveillance operations.

A PyPI supply chain attack targeted the data engineering community through a package impersonating a popular Apache Airflow plugin. The malicious package installed a reverse SSH tunnel during pip install, providing persistent remote access to data pipeline servers. The attack compromised database credentials and ETL configurations at over 200 organizations before removal.
